title: Make a drawer insert that fits the object you own
task: Turn a scan of an awkwardly shaped tool into a fitted drawer insert with somewhere to put your fingers.
prompt: Use this scan of [object] and my drawer dimensions to design a removable insert. Trace its footprint, try two orientations, and add a thumb scoop. Give me a dimensioned preview and a thin test piece before the full model.
check: Measure the reference length on the model and try the test piece with the actual object before printing the full insert.
sourceLabel: A maker’s printed mouse insert and CAD files
inputs: Object scan with a known scale, drawer measurements, slicer

title: Turn a favorite hike into printable terrain
task: Make a relief map that fits a frame and follows the actual hills along a memorable route.
prompt: Build a terrain model for [park or coordinates] using public elevation data. Show the map boundary, frame dimensions and vertical exaggeration. Return a mesh I can preview with the starting point marked on the accompanying map.
check: Find two known landmarks on the preview and check the overall dimensions in your slicer.
sourceLabel: Topo Shadow Box project and sample agent prompts
inputs: Area coordinates, desired frame size, public elevation data

title: Read your printer’s bed-level report
task: See which corner of a print bed sits high before turning any adjustment screws.
prompt: Use this saved bed mesh from [printer] to draw a labeled height map. Locate the largest deviation and explain which corner it represents from where I stand. Use the manual to identify the next measurement I should take.
check: Match the diagram’s front-left corner to the printer’s coordinate system. Take a second measurement before changing anything.
sourceLabel: r/ClaudeCode member’s printer-leveling project
inputs: Saved probe grid, printer model and manual

title: Make a private mail backup you can actually search
task: Build a read-only search view so an old receipt or conversation can be found even with the inbox offline.
prompt: Start with this small copy of my mail archive. Create a private search view with sender, date and subject filters. Let me open a full thread and find an attachment. Work only from the copied messages.
check: Disconnect from the mail service and find a known attachment and a reply from a different date. Check that the archive still contains the original messages.
sourceLabel: Andreas Gohr’s searchable mail backup
inputs: Local sample of an exported mailbox, trusted private workspace

title: Build a PDF page sorter that works offline
task: Create a small browser tool for removing cover sheets and reordering scanned pages without uploading the documents.
prompt: With [sample scan], make a local page sorter. I need thumbnails, undo, and a download containing just the pages I select, in that order. Use a harmless sample while developing it and show me which requests the page makes.
check: Disconnect the network after loading the tool. Export pages 4, 1 and 3, reopen the result, and check the order and number of pages.
sourceLabel: Hacker News maker’s browser-local PDF editor
inputs: Sample PDF, browser, private coding workspace

title: Shrink a screen recording until its text is barely affected
task: Find a GIF small enough for a help article while keeping the cursor and button labels legible.
prompt: Try several compression settings on this GIF of [workflow]. Give me synchronized previews and file sizes for the original and the three smallest candidates under [limit]. Preserve the timing of the final click.
check: Read the smallest label at its published size and watch the final click in both versions before picking one.
sourceLabel: Simon Willison’s browser GIF optimizer and build notes
inputs: Short GIF, upload size limit, target display width

title: Watch an algorithm make one decision at a time
task: Turn a hard-to-explain piece of code into a small animation you can pause at the exact decision that puzzles you.
prompt: Trace [algorithm] on this tiny input. Build a single-page view with Step, Back and Reset. Show what it tried, what it rejected and why. Link the important decisions to the original code.
check: Hand-trace three steps on paper and compare the final output with the original program.
sourceLabel: Simon Willison’s animated word-placement example
inputs: A small algorithm, source code, one reproducible input

title: Put every signup screen on one editable canvas
task: Give designers the current signup journey, including the screens people see when something goes wrong.
prompt: Walk through [staging signup] with a test account. Capture the empty form, validation error, permission request and success state in a new design file. Arrange editable frames in order and mark the step where the app first asks for personal information.
check: Compare each frame with the running app and edit a single button label on the canvas to confirm it is editable.
sourceLabel: Figma’s live UI to editable canvas guide
inputs: Test account, staging URL, editable Figma draft

title: Find the step that traps a keyboard user
task: Get a repeatable account of where someone loses focus or gets stuck in a form without a mouse.
prompt: Start on [staging form] and complete it using only the keyboard. Open and dismiss each dialog. Record the key sequence and accessible name at the first point you cannot continue, then locate the responsible element in the source.
check: Follow the written keystrokes yourself. Check that closing a dialog restores focus to the control that opened it.
sourceLabel: GitHub Next’s browser-based accessibility review
inputs: Staging URL, keyboard or browser control, optional source access

title: Rehearse guest checkout before a release
task: Turn one checkout journey into a repeatable browser test that catches a lost cart or an unexpected charge.
prompt: Explore guest checkout on [test store]. Write down its steps, then make a browser test for each outcome: accepted test card, declined test card, and going back to edit the quantity. Keep the fake order IDs as evidence.
check: Run from a fresh session twice. Check the cart total, confirmation state and test-order count after each scenario.
sourceLabel: Playwright’s planner, generator and healer workflow
inputs: Test storefront, test payment method, disposable carts

title: Find what a slow page is waiting for
task: Separate a slow image download from the time a browser spends waiting to draw it.
prompt: Record a loading trace for [page] using the same phone profile three times. Identify the largest visible element, when its request starts and when it appears. Propose one change and repeat the measurement on a preview build.
check: Compare the median of the three runs using the same cache setting and network profile. Check that the visible element stayed the same.
sourceLabel: Chrome DevTools’ agent performance walkthrough
inputs: Public or staging page, browser performance tracing

title: Turn a failed browser request into a reproducible bug
task: Give the person fixing a broken button the exact request and UI steps that trigger it.
prompt: In my test browser, inspect the failed request from [button]. Trace what initiated it, compare it with one successful request, and produce the shortest reproduction with a sanitized response excerpt. Keep cookies, tokens and personal data out of the report.
check: Recreate the failure from a clean test session using only the report. Confirm the redacted request still shows the meaningful difference.
sourceLabel: Chrome DevTools’ live network-request investigation
inputs: Test session with a repeatable failure, browser network inspector

title: Explain a cloud data-transfer bill
task: Trace a jump in bandwidth charges to the resource and traffic route that account for it.
prompt: For [billing dates], compare transfer charges with the previous equivalent period. Break the increase down by account, region and usage type. Follow the largest change into available flow records and show how much of the increase remains unexplained.
check: Reconcile the subtotal with the billing export and match one traffic sample to the proposed resource. Leave the infrastructure untouched.
sourceLabel: AWS sample cost-analysis agent and transfer investigation
inputs: Read-only billing export and optional network-flow records

title: Tell a database bottleneck from a sudden burst of traffic
task: Find which event happened first when several services started timing out together.
prompt: For [alert window], line up request volume, time waiting for a database connection, pool occupancy and slow queries. Test both explanations: more requests arrived, or existing requests held connections longer. Return the timeline and links to the decisive graphs.
check: Pick an unaffected service as a comparison and verify the order of events against the raw timestamps.
sourceLabel: Grafana’s internal connection-pool incident
inputs: Read-only service dashboards, incident window, database metrics

title: Locate the part of an AI service that is failing
task: See whether failures cluster around one provider region or model before paging the whole team.
prompt: Group [redacted failed requests] by provider, model, region and time. Compute the error rate using total attempts for each group. Compare unaffected regions and recent changes. Return the smallest affected group plus evidence for or against a provider incident.
check: Match the suspected group to raw traces, check traffic volume, and corroborate a provider outage before assigning cause.
sourceLabel: Sentry’s account of a regional model outage
inputs: Redacted request traces with attempt counts and region labels

title: Make a file reader survive malformed input
task: Exercise a neglected part of a parser and leave behind a tiny file that reproduces any crash.
prompt: In an isolated test checkout of our parser, target [format feature] that our existing tests rarely reach. Generate a small fuzz harness and seed files, test with a resource limit, and shrink any crashing input. Save coverage before and after.
check: Replay the minimized input outside the harness. Verify the crash belongs to the parser before filing a private report with its owner.
sourceLabel: Google’s OSS-Fuzz team on generating fuzz targets
inputs: Authorized parser source, test corpus, isolated build environment

title: Try a risky library upgrade on one representative service
task: Learn what a fleet-wide migration will break before asking every team to update.
prompt: Choose one service that exercises [old API] in typical and unusual ways. Migrate it in a branch, find call sites that need different treatment, and run the same checks as its regular build. Return a patch and a list of exceptions for the next service.
check: Have the service owner run its integration test on the old and new versions. Expand to a second service only after reviewing the differences.
sourceLabel: Spotify Engineering’s Honk migration case study
inputs: Service inventory, approved test repository, upgrade guide

title: See which dashboards a data-model change would affect
task: Preview the downstream reports and totals that would move if you changed a shared model.
prompt: For [proposed model edit], trace its dependent models and columns. Build the changed model in a development schema, compare old and new values, and name the first downstream report where the difference becomes visible.
check: Check row counts and totals on the same dated sample. Ask the owner of the affected metric to confirm whether the change is intended.
sourceLabel: dbt’s worked example of a model change and data diff
inputs: Model project, lineage metadata, read-only baseline, development schema

title: Find why the same sales question gets two answers
task: Turn a disagreement over a metric into a definition and a query your analysts can check.
prompt: Take these anonymized questions about [metric] and the queries the analytics assistant used. Group answers that disagree. Show which definition, filter or time window changed, ask the metric owner to resolve it, and rerun the original questions.
check: Compare the new answers with an analyst-verified query for the same period, including a zero-sales day.
sourceLabel: Snowflake’s workflow for reviewing analytics-agent answers
inputs: Anonymized question logs, query definitions, metric owner

title: Recover a business rule buried in a legacy program
task: Give the people replacing an old system a decision table they can verify against its actual behavior.
prompt: Trace [one discount or eligibility rule] from its entry point through the old code and input records. Make a decision table with conditions, outcomes and source lines. Highlight branches that require a business owner to interpret them.
check: Replay approved historical examples just below, at and above a threshold. Check the table against the old program’s results.
sourceLabel: AWS’s mainframe business-rule extraction walkthrough
inputs: Legacy source, data layout, representative approved examples

title: Add a payment option without missing its failure states
task: Use an existing payment method as a reference for implementing another in a test checkout.
prompt: Compare [new method] with the closest existing one in this codebase. Trace configuration, API types and UI state. Draft a sandbox integration and exercise a successful payment, cancellation and a delayed confirmation where supported.
check: Use the provider’s test environment. Verify the order switches to paid only after the expected confirmation.
sourceLabel: Stripe’s payment-method integration case study
inputs: Existing integration, provider’s test documentation, sandbox account

title: Catch behavior changes in a project you depend on
task: Spot an upstream change before a library, adapter or plug-in silently stops matching it.
prompt: Review the commits since [upstream version] that touch features my adapter supports. For one plausible change, port the smallest upstream test to my branch and run it against both implementations. Return a compatibility table with the first disagreement.
check: Reproduce the same case on the stated upstream release and on the adapter. Record both versions beside the result.
sourceLabel: Cloudflare’s upstream compatibility checks for Vinext
inputs: Upstream and adapter source, supported-version list, test environment

title: Check whether a web feature will strand older browsers
task: Build an evidence table for a feature before relying on it in a customer-facing page.
prompt: Look up [feature] in a versioned copy of MDN’s browser compatibility data. Compare first support with our minimum desktop and mobile versions. Carry over flags, partial support and footnotes, then identify which customers still need a fallback.
check: Open the exact MDN entry and verify a flagged or partial-support row. Check one supported and one unsupported browser in staging.
sourceLabel: Simon Willison’s queryable browser-compatibility database
inputs: Feature name, supported browser versions, MDN compatibility data

title: Replay the moment a coding agent went off course
task: Turn a long agent session into a timeline showing the first wrong assumption and the change it caused.
prompt: Use this sanitized session export to make a local, searchable timeline of prompts, tool calls, results and file changes. Mark the first time the agent acted on [incorrect assumption]. Link that event to the resulting diff.
check: Pick three timeline events and compare them with their original records. Remove secrets and private paths before sharing any excerpt.
sourceLabel: Show HN author’s coding-session viewer
inputs: Sanitized session export, optional diff, private workspace

title: Find a build step worth making faster
task: Choose one expensive part of continuous integration and verify whether changing it saves enough time to matter.
prompt: Inspect recent successful builds on [workflow]. Separate queue time from runtime, identify repeated work on the slowest chain of steps, and propose one cache or job-order change. Include cold and warm comparisons on the same revision.
check: Check wall-clock duration and billed runner minutes separately. Confirm the proposed build still runs every required check.
sourceLabel: GitHub Next’s CI Coach workflow
inputs: Workflow definitions, recent job timings, test branch

title: Find where a replacement implementation disagrees with the original
task: Get one small input that proves two implementations behave differently, even when their normal tests pass.
prompt: Run [old and new implementation] on the same small generated inputs in a sandbox. Compare outputs, shrink the first difference, and identify which behavior the specification requires. Keep the input, versions and commands together.
check: Replay the example from a clean checkout, then add it to the test suite only after confirming the expected result.
sourceLabel: Nicholas Carlini’s compiler-testing experiment
inputs: Reference implementation, replacement, specification, bounded test environment

title: Build a phonics game around the sounds a child is learning
task: Give a beginning reader a tiny playable deck with words that match this week’s lesson.
prompt: Make an offline flashcard game from my list of [letter sounds]. Use the words and approved pictures I supply. Let a child reveal the word after trying it and let me repeat missed cards without collecting names or scores online.
check: Have the teacher check every word against the target sounds and try the deck on the device the child will use.
sourceLabel: Hacker News maker’s phonics game for their children
inputs: Teacher-approved word list, pictures, target device

title: Turn one of your chess losses into a personal lesson
task: Find the moment your plan went wrong by comparing your own thinking with a chess engine’s analysis.
inputs: A completed game in PGN format, optional voice notes, chess-engine access
prompt: Review this finished game alongside my notes. Pick three moments when my reasoning and the engine disagree. For each, show my plan, the opponent’s strongest reply and a diagram where I can try a different move before seeing the answer.
check: Replay each line on a board. Make sure the engine evaluated the exact position, side to move and legal replies shown in the lesson.
sourceLabel: Show HN maker’s chess coach using voice notes and Stockfish

title: Follow a disputed idea through books you already own
task: Build a reading trail that shows where authors give different explanations for the same event or idea.
inputs: Searchable books or personal highlights, edition details, one question
prompt: Search my reading collection for passages about [question]. Start with one author’s claim, find a second author who complicates it, then look for a counterexample in a third book. Give me a reading order, a short excerpt and a page or chapter locator for each stop.
check: Open each passage in its edition and read the paragraphs around it. Remove a connection if it depends on stripping that context.
sourceLabel: Show HN author’s experiment connecting passages across 100 books

title: Recover an old backup with a revived tape driver
task: Help a hardware specialist port an obsolete tape driver so a modern test machine can read a cartridge.
inputs: Driver source, kernel headers, spare test machine, known-good test cartridge
prompt: Trace the read path in [legacy driver]. Use these build errors and hardware logs to identify outdated kernel calls, then draft the smallest patch that lets a test rig read a write-protected cartridge. I will review and load the driver on the spare machine myself.
check: Detect the drive and read a known test tape twice. Compare both images with a known-good dump before a specialist handles the original cartridge.
sourceLabel: Dmitry Brant’s account of recovering tapes with ftape
